maximum_inference: At most, this visual explains the chapter's design rationale at argument support; it adds no empirical, deployment, safety, transfer, state-of-the-art, AGI, or ASI result.

required_content.problem: Capability-threshold policies require domain-specific evidence about whether a model can materially increase an actor's ability to cause harm, yet the stack has no owner for CBRN, offensive cyber, psychological manipulation, or the science of measuring model-caused uplift. Knowledge quizzes, refusal rates, benchmark scores, one red team, or a capability label cannot identify real actor uplift. They omit baseline expertise, tool and scaffold access, multi-step completion, bottlenecks outside the model, elicitation quality, safeguards, substitution, uncertainty, and the danger created by the evaluation itself.
required_content.core_mechanism: Dangerous-capability authority should be based on a versioned domain threat model and an uplift dossier that separates latent capability, elicited performance, propensity, safeguard bypass, actor uplift, and realized harm; preserves expertise, tools, assistance, attempts, uncertainty, and sensitive-detail boundaries; and routes only bounded findings into thresholds, release, monitoring, and resilience decisions. Decompose each domain into actor, objective, access, prerequisites, bottlenecks, model contribution, external controls, consequences, and safe evaluation envelope. Use controlled uplift studies that compare matched actors with and without bounded model assistance while stratifying prior expertise and preserving all attempts.
required_content.worked_trace: Create a public-safe threat-model and uplift-dossier format, then run a harmless analogue study with stratified participants or competent agents, matched assistance, known-positive and known-negative controls, blinded scoring, complete attempt logs, and no real hazardous materials or targets. Demonstrate that the instrument can distinguish a real assistance effect before using a null result. Use controlled uplift studies that compare matched actors with and without bounded model assistance while stratifying prior expertise and preserving all attempts. Triangulate knowledge, workflow, long-horizon, expert-probing, safeguard-bypass, and trend evaluations without collapsing them into one score.
required_content.failure_boundary: knowledge benchmark substituted for operational uplift refusal behavior substituted for latent capability expertise imbalance between arms weak elicitation or scaffold
required_content.evidence_state: This chapter remains Design rationale at argument support. Its contracts, examples, tests, or local artifacts establish only their encoded scope. A finite dangerous-capability dossier may hand off only when model, threat, cohort, access, evaluator, uncertainty, expiry, and maximum inference are present; no theorem establishes dangerous capability or safety. Every result is bound to an exact model, checkpoint, scaffold, tools, access level, actor cohort, domain, date, and evaluator. A negative result is interpretable only after positive-control, elicitation, sensitivity, and task-validity gates pass.
required_content.non_claims: No chapter claim or evidence state is promoted by this visual. A named mechanism is not proof of correct implementation or useful deployment. A local check or formal model does not establish real-world enforcement. No safety, transfer, state-of-the-art, AGI, or ASI conclusion follows.
